The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: Switching off a feature setting sent more shoppers' account pages through a spending calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 35.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 4,702.30 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #539 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while legacy-checkout-fallback was off
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:50 to 02:58 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 03:17:34 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:56:46 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 02:50 UTC and was back to normal at 02:58 UTC, 8 minutes later. 26.1% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 35.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 4,702.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching off a feature setting sent more shoppers' account pages through a spending calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #539, for a person to review and merge. Account page requests that still reach the monthly spend summary could fail for shoppers with no purchases this month, and switching legacy-checkout-fallback off again would bring the same failures back.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
35.5% - peak error rate
2,508 - requests failed
1.0% to 26.1% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
4,702.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
`average_spend_per_item_this_month` in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`, and it does not handle the case where that list is empty, which is the ordinary case for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. With legacy-checkout-fallback off, more account page requests went through `render_spend_summary`'s monthly path into this division, raised ZeroDivisionError, and `serve_account_page` turned each one into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's share of requests answered with server errors rose, and the service logged failed account page requests and warnings about the account page error rate.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 32 occurrences in 37 minutes, 02:20–02:56; # was 0.50% to 35.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 02:55
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:50–02:56
why 1 Those account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, and the account page turned each error into a failed page.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
why 2 At 02:50:38 UTC admin switched the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off. In the onset minute some account page requests already read the flag as off, every minute after that all of them did, and the ZeroDivisionError failures start in that same onset minute.
  Evidence:
    P1 02:50:38 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
    G7ad6 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 70 / on 130 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:50
    G7037 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:51–02:56
    G5309
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 02:51; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
    Some other flag change: the flag provider's history held a single change by anyone but Argus in the hour it read, and that change is this toggle.
      T14 02:57:16 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:57:16
      P1
    Shoppers closing the connection: those errors were already logged before the onset, at a time when the flag was on and account pages rendered normally.
      G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 38 occurrences in 30 minutes, 02:20–02:49
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 5 occurrences in 18 minutes, 02:22–02:39
      G153f INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 02:20–02:49
why 3 With the flag off, more account page requests went through render_spend_summary's monthly spend path, where average_spend_per_item_this_month divides by the number of this month's purchases, so it fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1
    G5309
Contributing factors
- No test was seen that covered average_spend_per_item_this_month, or render_spend_summary's monthly path, for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. The test file itself calls that the ordinary case. (AI-2)
- The production change to legacy-checkout-fallback went from a share of requests to all of them almost at once. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on rising errors were seen. (AI-3)
- No check was seen that exercised account pages with legacy-checkout-fallback off before it was switched off in production. (AI-4, AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off at 02:50:38 UTC. Account page requests then failed with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% to about 28-35%. No code or config was deployed. | 0.93 | confirmed

Trigger
legacy-checkout-fallback flag went from ON to OFF at 02:50:38 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:57:23 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 03:00:25 | Proposed a fix: PR #539 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:50 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 02:56:23 UTC, 6 minutes 23 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #539 | open
AI-3 | Make changes to io-shop feature flags roll out to a small share of requests first, and halt and revert them automatically when the error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a CI test that renders io-shop account pages with each feature flag both on and off, using a shopper with past purchases but none this month. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Require that the flag-state account page test passes before a flag on io-shop can be changed in production. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 53 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C1, moved from OFF to ON.
- 2 minutes 39 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes 2 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #539.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called in to respond.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Response effort
none - engineer time
171,183 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/3ea42cc0-5506-4ba9-b8f3-07023d43c96c
The fix it proposed: PR #539 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/539) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 02:50:38 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G153f | INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 02:20–02:49
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 38 occurrences in 30 minutes, 02:20–02:49
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 32 occurrences in 37 minutes, 02:20–02:56; # was 0.50% to 35.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 02:55
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 5 occurrences in 18 minutes, 02:22–02:39
G7ad6 | INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 70 / on 130 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:50
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:50–02:56
G7037 | INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:51–02:56
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py builds the list of purchases with in_current_month set, then divides account.total_this_month_cents by that list's length. When the list is empty, that is a division by zero. An empty list is normal: it covers any shopper who has bought before but not this month, which tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls "the ordinary case". render_spend_summary sends a request to this function whenever use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false. So every request in that slice, for a shopper with no purchases this month, raised ZeroDivisionError. serve_account_page in src/io_shop/account_page.py catches it at its boundary and turns it into a failed page. The flag change only changed how many requests took that path. The division itself was always wrong.

The fix: if nothing was bought this month, the function now returns 0, meaning nothing spent per item this month. Otherwise it divides exactly as before. The return type stays int, so the function signature, render_spend_summary and its callers are unchanged. The lifetime average is untouched. Its divisor can still be zero for an account with no purchases at all, and the existing test that expects that error to reach the caller still holds. Errors are not hidden anywhere else: only the empty-month case is handled, and it is handled with a value rather than an exception.

The tests: in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py I added two. One calls average_spend_per_item_this_month directly, and the other goes through render_spend_summary(use_monthly_summary=True). Both use a shopper with past purchases but none this month and assert the figure is 0. Both are written to raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist

✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)

○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not load their account pages, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. The trouble began when a feature setting was switched off. That sent more shoppers' account pages through a spending calculation that divides by the number of purchases made this month, so it likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. No one was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus reverted the feature setting, legacy-checkout-fallback. That change is confirmed and still in place. Argus also proposed a fix to the calculation as PR #539. It is open as a draft and has not been put into service.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
